title: Oboe
summary: Limits first: the reed is assembled, not measured; its mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed. Which pages play now (2026-11-10, after the owner's restore of earlier renders): Bb4 is the 2026-11-04 22:57Z noise-row render (binary 4112efef27b0, BEFORE the closure stop: 450.6 Hz, 59 c flat of equal temperament and 61.3 c flat of the recording, 7 of 15, strict 7; it carries no stop, no tongue row, no contraction row, no bore air profile, no mutual hole radiation and no printed hole lengths, and every paragraph below that gives Bb4 after the stop or with those rows, such as 494.45 Hz and 6 of 15, describes the later page, which stays in the page's history and does not play); Db4 is the 2026-11-07 09:17Z discontinuous-Galerkin render at the 9.6 kHz design band (degree 2, 51 elements, up to 48 poles, 50 Hz to 9.6 kHz; 276.58 Hz, 3.8 c flat of equal temperament and 7.4 c sharp of the recording, 8 of 15, strict 5; it carries no tongue row), and the paragraphs below that give Db4 on the converged 20 kHz bore or with the tongue row, such as 6 of 14, describe the later pages, also in the page's history. F4 is the 2026-11-10 15:33Z render of the card with the printed reed volumes and the staple pressure recovery (item 7 near the end: 6 of 15, strict 6, D 15.79; 352.78 Hz, 17.7 c sharp of the recording), and the paragraphs below that give F4 at 356 Hz, or with the tongue area 6.979e-5, the lay stiffness 5.7437e6, the Strasser bell or no staple row, describe the pages before it, in the page's history. Recording property, Db4: the recording's own floor after the note is about -49.5 dB re the note's power (median floor, 0.1 to 10 kHz, read on the 0.1 s after the note), 12 % of the noise power its harmonics-to-noise reading counts (40.4 dB); the page reads 63.4 dB, 22.9 dB above the recording, and that floor alone would hold a perfectly periodic note to about 49.5 dB; the rest of the recording's noise is in the note and its source is not identified, and period jitter, shimmer and slow pitch movement of the recording are worth at most 2.3 dB of it. Since the reed's closure stop (a857c6f17) the scale sits -7 to +33 c from equal temperament (F4 at its printed pressure only); before it, 22 to 158 c flat. At the pages' 7.4 kPa F4 plays an octave up (677 Hz). The old flat scale was the reed passing through its lay. The tongue is a labelled borrowed-number row (`tongue_contact`, described near the end) on the F4, D5 and Ab5 pages and is not on the G5, D4, Bb4 and Db4 pages that play (the D4 page, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, carries none; the tongue was tried there, below; the restored Bb4 and Db4 pages carry none, and the later pages that did are in their histories); only the first open hole has a nonlinear loss, a quasi-steady orifice (all eleven open holes on the D5 page, `open_hole_orifice 11`, all five on the F4 page, `open_hole_orifice 5`, and all nine on the Ab5 page, `open_hole_orifice 9`; all three on the D4 page, whose discontinuous-Galerkin card carries `dg_terminal_orifice 0.61` on its three open chimneys; the Db4 page, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, has no orifice law at all), and the breath noise row on Bb4, Db4, D4, F4, D5, G5 and Ab5 drives only 10 to 20 kHz on this reed's 0.87 mm duct. A C major scale and Ode to Joy are up, each note its own render at the pages' 7.4 kPa except F4, at its printed 6865 Pa, on fingerings inferred from Table III of Nederveen and de Bruijn 1967, the one complete oboe tone-hole table this project holds. Bb4 (6 of 15, strict 5, with the contraction, profile, interaction and length rows below) is a graded page re-rendered after the stop, Db4 (6 of 14, strict 4, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore at its converged 20 kHz band, observed to 9.6 kHz, below) is a graded page, and Bb4 sounds as B4, 102 c sharp of its name; G5 sounds at its written octave (790.90 Hz, G5 +15.2 c) on a card with a re-specified octave vent, and has no grade; Ab5 sounds at its written octave as a single series (819.53 Hz, Ab5 -23.3 c) on a card with a re-specified octave vent, and has no grade and no count (below); D4, F4 and D5 are first pages at their printed pressures. A staple pressure recovery row (Almeida, Vergez and Caussé 2007; C_P 0.8 and S_c 4 mm^2, one measured reed's two numbers, borrowed; commit b57b46619) is on the D4, D5 and F4 pages (F4: item 7 near the end): D4, which does not speak at 6178 Pa without it, speaks with it (301.95 Hz, 48 c sharp of D4, on the first staple page; ungraded, a listening page). The D5 page also carries the clarinet's bore air temperature profile (Noreland 2013, measured on a clarinet and borrowed for the oboe, positions rescaled), the mutual radiation impedance of the open holes and the bell, the printed thick-wall hole lengths of Lefebvre and Scavone, and, as a labelled bound trial, a jet contraction row (`contraction 0.611`, the two-dimensional free-streamline bound pi/(pi+2); commit 25b9bc64c): no double-reed value is printed; the card's reed area (2.0 mm^2) is Almeida's printed typical oboe rest area, not their fitted 3.05 to 3.37 mm^2, so the reed they measured passes more flow than the card's (peak 249 to 313 mL/s against 132, and 81 with the row), 0.611 is a borrowed value and not a coefficient of this reed; the channel's unsteady inertance has no printed effective length and is not in the row. With those five rows the page sounded at 578.17 Hz, D5 -27.2 c (from -73.1 c without any of them, and 571.12 Hz, -48.5 c, with the first four), and scored 5 of 14, 3 on the strict ruler, against 4 and 3 for the page without the contraction row: the row brought the spectral flux inside the loose ruler, while the spectral distance, the third-octave envelope, the harmonic levels, the wavelet and cepstral gaps, odd against even and the centroid all widened, and the page was 5.1 dB quieter (96.5 dB SPL against 101.6). The D5 page now carries `open_hole_orifice 11` (commit 43ad828c9; it carried `open_hole_orifice 3` from commit 043f9b8e9 until then): the quasi-steady orifice loss of all eleven open holes (158 to 539 mm from the reed) solved together through the bore, each hole's coefficient from the gas at that hole, with two stated approximations: each orifice sees its own uncoupled radiation load, not the coupled one of the interaction row, and the sound the holes radiate still comes from the linear network, as for the first hole alone; the fully coupled orifice network is not built. With the loss on the first three holes the page sounded at 579.51 Hz, D5 -23.2 c, and scored 6 of 14, 5 on the strict ruler, against 5 and 3 for the page without the orifice row: the pitch came inside both rulers and the spectral flux inside the strict one, the waveform locked slightly less (autocorrelation 0.992 against 1.000), and the page was 0.3 dB quieter (96.2 dB SPL against 96.5); the render took 2.2 times the CPU. Three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so the cap is now twelve and the row takes every open hole: on all eleven the page sounds at 579.77 Hz, D5 -22.4 c, the level and the harmonic levels H1 to H8 are the same to the digit shown (96.2 dB SPL), and the count stays 6 of 14, 5 on the strict ruler, with seven gaps to the recording slightly larger (harmonics-to-noise 1.04 to 1.20 dB, spectral flux 0.78 to 0.92 dB, centroid, spectral distance, envelope, harmonic levels, STFT) and four slightly smaller (wavelet, cepstral envelope, pitch, odd against even); the render takes 1118 s of CPU against 591 s for the three-hole page, far less than the growth of the realized kernels (15 to 143) would give. The same card without the staple row scored 5 of 14, so on D5 the staple row costs one measure (spectral flux) and brings the pitch 15 c nearer the recording. The staple row lowered the count on Db4 (3 to 2) and Bb4 (6 to 5), so those pages stay without it. The contraction row (0.611, the same bound trial as on D5, on the live card with no other row) raised the Db4 count from 3 to 4 of 14 and the strict count stayed at 3: that page sounded at 280.73 Hz, 22.0 c sharp of Db4 and 33.1 c sharp of the recording (the page without the row, 275.08 Hz, was 2.0 c from the recording), so the pitch measure was lost from both rulers and odd against even from the strict one, while the partial frequencies and the attack came inside both rulers and the harmonics-to-noise reading flipped from 27.6 dB below the recording to 14.0 dB above it; the page was 4.8 dB quieter (97.8 dB SPL against 102.6) and the spectral, envelope, harmonic-level and wavelet gaps widened slightly. With `open_hole_orifice 3` as well (the card's only three open holes, 463, 499 and 539 mm from the reed, solved together, with the two approximations named on D5) that page kept 4 of 14, strict 3, at 280.80 Hz, +22.4 c from Db4 and 33.5 c sharp of the recording, 97.7 dB SPL: the row moved almost nothing on this note, and the cause is not known. The transfer-matrix Db4 page (replaced since by the discontinuous-Galerkin page described after it) carried the contraction row with the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths, and not the orifice row: it sounded at 274.99 Hz, 13.8 c flat of Db4 and 2.7 c flat of the recording, and scored 6 of 14, strict 6, against 4 and 3 for the page it replaced (and 3 and 3 for the original page): pitch, odd against even and harmonics-to-noise (41.4 dB against the recording's 40.4) came inside both rulers, while the cepstral envelope, partial trajectory, partial frequency and spectral flux moved slightly farther, and the page was 1.0 dB quieter (96.7 dB SPL against 97.7). The orifice row put on top of those four rows lowered it to 5 of 14, strict 5 (the harmonics-to-noise gap went from 0.92 to 2.81 dB and left both rulers; the cepstral envelope, 15.37 to 16.46 dB, and odd against even, 0.05 to 0.32 dB, were worse and stayed inside; the pitch, 2.69 to 2.59 c, and the level, 96.65 to 96.67 dB SPL, did not move; the render took 1884 s of CPU against 778), so the orifice row stayed off that page, the one oboe page that dropped it from its posted card. The Db4 page was, until the converged bore described after this paragraph, the discontinuous-Galerkin render at the 9.6 kHz design band (degree 2, 51 elements, wall memory to 9.6 kHz, the twenty chimneys as ducts, a sparse Krylov propagator, the reed as one lumped mode on a penalty contact, the bell and open holes as one computed baffled-piston array, the contraction row and the clarinet's air profile, no printed hole lengths, no orifice): it sounds at 276.58 Hz, 3.8 c flat of Db4 and 7.4 c sharp of the recording (the page it replaces: 2.7 c flat), steady to 0.0 c, 93.2 dB SPL (3.4 dB below), and scores 7 of 14, strict 4, against 6 and 6: spectral distance (26.05 to 12.68 dB) and harmonic levels (15.80 to 9.36 dB) come inside the loose ruler and harmonics-to-noise leaves it, and on the strict ruler odd against even and harmonics-to-noise leave, so the strict count falls from 6 to 4 while the loose count rises by one. It is too clean: harmonics-to-noise 63.4 dB against the recording's 40.4 (the page it replaces read 41.4). The pitch gap grows from 2.69 to 7.38 c, odd against even from 0.05 to 5.90 dB, the partial trajectory from 11.53 to 14.81 dB, the attack from 1.61 to 1.95 (log2) and the spectral flux from 2.04 to 2.25 dB, while the third-octave envelope (20.71 to 8.55 dB), the cepstral envelope (15.37 to 7.98), the wavelet (23.48 to 17.42) and STFT (30.66 to 26.43) gaps and the centroid (13.82 to 8.41 st) shrink; the render takes 11862 s of CPU on ts2. It posts by the loose count, with the strict fall and the too-clean note named on its page. The Db4 page now is the same card on the converged bore: only the `dg_bore` header changed, the degree of the elements 2 to 3, the wall poles 48 to 60, the band edge 9.6 to 20 kHz, the DOF cap 20480 to 32768 and the wall quadrature 3 to 4, observed to 9.6 kHz as before (the band edge did not matter: a 14 kHz bore pilot renders the 20 kHz bore's waveform to one 16-bit step; the other four changed together and were not isolated, so which of them moved the band energy is not shown). The 9.6 kHz bore was not converged: on the converged bore the same note holds 7.8 dB more energy in 1.5 to 4.8 kHz and 7.2 dB more in 4.8 to 9.6 kHz (steady 1 to 2 s, re total: -22.23 and -29.18 dB on the 9.6 kHz bore, -14.43 and -21.99 dB on the converged one; the recording -8.95 and -41.25 dB). It sounds at 276.57 Hz, Db4 -3.8 c and 7.3 c sharp of the recording (the 9.6 kHz bore 276.59 Hz), at 93.4 dB SPL (peak 3.38 Pa), and scores 6 of 14, strict 4, on lib1, the library that reproduces the live pair (lib0139 reads the 9.6 kHz bore 8 of 14, strict 5, and this render 6 and 4): the loose count falls by one because the spectral distance leaves the loose ruler (12.68 to 15.73 dB), and the strict count is unchanged, the same four measures inside. Gaps to the recording that grow: spectral distance 12.68 to 15.73 dB, third-octave envelope 8.55 to 11.27, harmonic levels 9.36 to 10.98, STFT 26.43 to 28.94, wavelet 17.42 to 19.57, partial frequency 0.29 to 0.39 c, and by under 0.05 the cepstral envelope, odd against even and partial trajectory; gaps that shrink: harmonics-to-noise 22.94 to 16.10 dB (the note reads 56.5 dB clean against the recording's 40.4, still too clean), centroid 8.41 to 6.26 st and spectral flux 2.25 to 2.04. The 4.8 to 9.6 kHz band now holds 19.3 dB more energy than the recording's, where the 9.6 kHz bore held 12.1 dB more, and the 1.5 to 4.8 kHz band is 5.5 dB under the recording's, where it was 13.3 dB under. The render took 33 554 s of CPU on K9 (11 862 s on the 9.6 kHz bore, on an earlier binary). It posts as the resolution fix it is, the 9.6 kHz bore not being converged, and not by its count. The Db4 page now carries the tongue row on that converged bore (`tongue_contact 1.12e-5 6.979e-5 0.2 0.1845 0.005` after the contraction row, the reed starting held at its equilibrium under the tongue, commit 48bab7995; rendered on bw18e, built before that commit's merge with the tip, in 30 256 s of wall time and 29 713.70 s of CPU): it is silent before the blow, every sample of 0 to 0.15 s exactly 0.0 as on the page without the row, with the first sample that differs at 154.7 ms; the steady tone is the same to the digits shown (276.572 Hz against 276.570 Hz, 0.9298 Pa against 0.9299 Pa, the three band energies -0.19, -14.43 and -21.99 dB on both) and the time to half of the steady level falls from 242.6 to 230.1 ms. It scores 6 of 14, strict 4, as the page without the row, no flag changing, so the count ties; the attack gap grows from 1.95 to 2.10 (log2; the attack time falls from 38.6 to 34.7 ms against the recording's 149.2 ms) and harmonics-to-noise from 16.10 to 16.19 dB, and seven gaps shrink by at most 0.04 (STFT 28.94 to 28.93, wavelet 19.57 to 19.55, cepstral envelope 8.03 to 8.02, partial trajectory 14.82 to 14.79, odd against even 5.94 to 5.93, centroid 6.26 to 6.25 st, spectral flux 2.04 to 2.00). It posts by the tie rule for an opt-in row, a result that did not help being shown and not hidden; its row is the one the Bb4, F4, D5 and Ab5 pages carry, with the support stated in the tongue paragraph near the end. The Bb4 page first carried three of those groups without the staple row: the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes (the doubled hole, holes 8 and 9 at one axial station, is coupled at its touching distance since commit 418a8f86b; before it the engine refused) and the printed hole lengths. It scored 6 of 15 against 6, a tie on the loose ruler, and 4 against 5 on the strict ruler (spectral flux left it), sounded 8.8 c sharper (496.22 Hz) and 0.87 dB quieter, and eight gaps to the recording moved slightly farther, against hundredths gained; with the staple row added it fell to 5 of 15. The Bb4 page now carries the contraction row as well (0.611, borrowed, a bound trial, no staple row, no orifice row): it sounds at 494.45 Hz, 102.0 c sharp of Bb4 and 99.6 c sharp of the recording, and scores 6 of 15, strict 5, against 6 and 4 for the page it replaces and 6 and 5 for the original page: spectral flux comes back inside the strict ruler, while the spectral distance, third-octave envelope, harmonic levels, cepstral envelope, odd against even and centroid move slightly farther, and the STFT and wavelet gaps, the pitch gap (105.8 to 99.6 c), harmonics-to-noise and attack move nearer; the page is 4.0 dB quieter (99.6 dB SPL against 103.6). On the original card the contraction row alone lowered the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4); together with the three groups it ties the loose count and gains a strict measure, so it is on the Bb4 page. The orifice row (`open_hole_orifice 3`, which solves the doubled hole with its neighbour) on the live Bb4 card lowered the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4; spectral flux leaves both rulers). Put on top of the four-row Bb4 page it lowers the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4; spectral flux leaves both rulers, 0.95 to 1.28 dB), moves the pitch 13.4 c lower and the level 1.03 dB lower, and takes 498 s of CPU against 222, so the orifice row stays off Bb4, as on Db4. On F4 the staple row alone moved the register edge below the printed pressure (676 Hz, the second register, at 6865 Pa), so the staple row alone stayed off F4 on that card; on the split card of 2026-11-10 it plays the first register and is on the F4 page (item 7 near the end). The contraction row alone (0.611, on the live card with no other row) keeps F4 in the first register at its printed 6865 Pa and raises the count from 5 to 6 of 15, strict 5 to 6: that page sounded at 352.49 Hz, F4 +16.1 c (the page without the row, 350.37 Hz, +5.7 c), gained the cepstral envelope and the harmonics-to-noise gap (11.5 to 5.7 dB) inside both rulers and lost spectral flux from both, while the pitch gap widened from 5.8 to 16.3 c, the partial-trajectory and attack gaps widened, and the page was 3.3 dB quieter (98.0 dB SPL against 101.3). With `open_hole_orifice 3` as well (the card's first three open holes, 351, 365 and 431 mm from the reed, solved together, with the two approximations named on D5) that page kept 6 of 15, strict 6, at 352.52 Hz, F4 +16.2 c, 97.8 dB SPL: the row moved almost nothing on this note, and the cause is not known. The F4 page now also carries the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths: it sounds at 354.18 Hz, F4 +24.4 c, and scores 6 of 15, strict 6, level with the page it replaces (no measure changes side of either ruler; the original page was 5 and 5): the pitch gap grows from 16.4 to 24.5 c, the spectral distance, third-octave envelope, STFT, partial trajectory, harmonics-to-noise, attack and spectral flux move slightly farther, the harmonic levels, wavelet, cepstral envelope and centroid slightly nearer, and the page is 0.6 dB quieter (97.2 dB SPL against 97.8); the render takes 990 s of CPU against 421 for the page without the orifice row. The F4 page now carries `open_hole_orifice 5` (commit 43ad828c9; it carried `open_hole_orifice 3` from commit 043f9b8e9 until then): the same orifice loss on all five open holes (351 to 539 mm from the reed), solved together; three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so this is a consistency fix. It sounds at 354.19 Hz, F4 +24.4 c, 97.2 dB SPL, and scores 6 of 15, strict 6, level with the three-hole page (no measure changes side of either ruler): the tone moves by 0.05 c, and the level and the harmonic levels H1 to H8 are the same to the digit shown. Four gaps to the recording grew slightly (partial trajectory 19.76 to 19.99 dB, pitch 24.55 to 24.59 c, harmonics-to-noise 6.92 to 6.93 dB, spectral flux 2.36 to 2.39 dB) and four shrank (cepstral envelope, partial frequency, odd against even, centroid); the render takes 1072 s of CPU against 935 s for the three-hole page on the same build. With the staple row and the contraction row together the note also stays in the first register (353.23 Hz) and scores 5 of 15, strict 5, level with the page without them. Ab5 is posted at its written octave with the contraction row (0.611, the bound trial of the D5 page; no staple row), the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes, the printed hole lengths, `open_hole_orifice 9` (all nine open holes, 129 to 539 mm from the reed; until commit 43ad828c9 the page carried `open_hole_orifice 3`, the vent and holes 11 and 12, because three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so the nine-hole row is a consistency fix), the tongue row `tongue_contact` (described near the end) and the octave vent, hole 2, re-specified to a bore of 0.81 mm and a height of 0.7 mm, the same vent as the G5 page (its numbers and sources are in the G5 paragraph; the old 6 mm height was an assumption copied from hole 3, and the depth stands on the repo's citation of a maker's page only). With that vent it sounds at 819.53 Hz, Ab5 -23.3 c and 30.5 c flat of the recording's 834.08 Hz, a single steady series (the strongest line holds the pitch to 0.00 c across 0.3 to 2.3 s; autocorrelation at the pitch's own period 0.970 with the period moving 2.3 c, at the doubled period 0.997), at 100.8 dB SPL (peak 6.45 Pa), and the clip no longer falls back to the first register at its end (the last strong line is 816 Hz); harmonics-to-noise reads 49.3 dB against the recording's 43.0. With the old 0.3 mm by 6 mm vent the same card sounded at 817.20 Hz, Ab5 -28.2 c and 35.4 c flat of the recording, as a period doubling and not a clean note: the line at half the frequency, 408.69 Hz, stood 25.3 dB under the pitch line (autocorrelation at the pitch's own period 0.461 with the period moving 174 c; at the doubled period 0.957 and 0.5 c), at 99.2 dB SPL, with the last 0.15 s falling back toward 411 Hz as the blowing pressure released; the page before it (the card with the vent and the closure stop and none of these rows) sounded an octave down at 411.32 Hz, Ab4 -16.7 c, and the three-hole page sounded at 817.12 Hz, also period-doubled. Without the orifice row the note is not clean either (lines at 835.7, 1262.3, 1671.4, 2489.1 and 2507.1 Hz within 5 dB of each other; autocorrelation 0.877 at 417.84 Hz with the period moving 37 c); that was read with the old vent and not repeated with the new one. Ab5 has no ruler, so there is no grade and no count: its tests are the register against the written note, whether it speaks and locks, and the level; correcting the vent's assumed height removes the period doubling and the fall back, and the clip is 1.6 dB louder (peak 6.45 Pa against 5.40). G5 is posted at its written octave, on the `g4c` card (the contraction row, the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths) with the octave vent, hole 2, re-specified from the printed 0.3 mm bore and the assumed 6 mm height to a bore of 0.81 mm and a height of 0.7 mm: it sounds at 790.90 Hz, G5 +15.2 c and 12.7 c sharp of the recording's 785.13 Hz, a single steady series (autocorrelation 0.981 with the period moving 2.2 c, the strongest line holding to 0.03 c), at 100.8 dB SPL (peak 6.86 Pa), where the page it replaces sounded an octave down at 398.35 Hz (autocorrelation 0.956 with the period moving 0.8 c; 103.4 dB SPL, peak 12.24 Pa). The same card with the old vent is not a note: two tones 15.3 Hz apart at 387.4 and 402.7 Hz (G4 -20 c and +45 c) with their second harmonics, the strongest line jumping between about 1193 and 2364 Hz from one 100 ms slice to the next, autocorrelation 0.907 with the period moving 40 c; with `open_hole_orifice 3` as well the strongest line holds 783.4 Hz (the written G5) in every slice, but the waveform does not repeat at that frequency (autocorrelation 0.327) and repeats near 394 Hz, an octave down, with autocorrelation 0.743 and the period moving 31 c; so the old vent never reached the written octave. The vent's numbers, as they stand: the bore range 0.66 to 0.81 mm is the patent's print (US 6,124,537); the depth 0.7 mm and the ranges 0.5 to 0.7 mm (bore) and 0.25 to 0.7 mm (depth) are S. Fox's maker's page as the repo's notes cite it, and stand on that citation only, because the page could not be retrieved; the old 6 mm height was an assumption copied from hole 3, and the old 0.3 mm bore is Table III's printed but doubtful value. The point (0.405 mm radius, 0.7 mm height) was declared before any render, and the page posts because all three corners of the sourced range reach the written octave: 792.57 Hz (radius 0.25 mm, height 0.25 mm), 791.75 Hz (0.35 mm, 0.7 mm) and 790.92 Hz (0.405 mm, 0.7 mm), the pitch falling 1.7 c per step as the vent opens. Hand arithmetic, not the engine's law, puts the old vent at 42 to 57 times the bore's characteristic impedance at its station, an almost closed hole, and the three sourced vents at 0.65 to 1.7 times. The Woodwind Fingering Guide's chart gives G5 as G4's fingering plus the first (thumb) octave key; which of holes 1, 2 and 5 that key opens is not printed, and hole 2 was chosen by position (a semi-automatic oboe lets the thumb key work either vent). Harmonics-to-noise reads 49.2 dB against the old page's 57.4 (the recording 36.5) and spectral flux 3.45 dB against 2.88 (the recording 2.42). G5 has no ruler, so there is no grade and no count. The paragraph from here to the one on the converged bore describes the earlier D4 page, on the reed-performance route, which the converged-bore page replaces; it carried, besides its staple row, the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes, the printed hole lengths and `open_hole_orifice 3` (all three of its open holes, 431, 499 and 539 mm from the reed) and the tongue row `tongue_contact` (described near the end), and not the contraction row: added to the staple, profile, interaction and length rows it silences D4 at 6178 Pa, with or without the orifice row (peak 0.03 Pa, lock 0.13), so it stays off D4. The D4 page sounds at 303.78 Hz, more than 50 c sharp of D4 and so nearer Eb4 than D4 (the page it replaces, 301.96 Hz, sat 48 c sharp of D4), steady (autocorrelation 1.000, the period moving 0.1 c), at 101.4 dB SPL, 0.81 dB under the page it replaces (102.2 dB SPL). Its pitch gap to the recording (294.04 Hz) grows from 46.02 to 56.46 c: 10.1 c of the 10.4 c step comes from the profile, interaction and length rows and 0.3 c from the orifice row, which also costs 911 s of CPU against 369 without it and 116 for the page it replaces. D4 has no ruler, so there is no count and no grade, and the page is a listening page. The gaps to the recording that grow, from regrade.py on lib0139: pitch, spectral distance (32.17 to 32.93 dB), third-octave envelope (22.67 to 23.47), harmonic levels (22.84 to 23.10), STFT (38.62 to 38.98), spectral flux (1.02 to 1.44) and harmonics-to-noise (6.35 to 13.03 dB: the page reads 55.3 dB against the recording's 42.3, 13 dB too clean, and about 7 dB of that rise comes from the orifice row, cause not known); the wavelet, cepstral envelope, odd against even, attack and centroid gaps shrink slightly, and partial trajectory and partial frequency do not move. The rows on Ab5 and D4 were rendered together, so what each does alone was not measured there. S_c = 4 mm^2 is corroborated: the mold of Almeida, Vergez and Causse 2007 (Fig. 14) reads 4.2 mm^2 at the constriction (28.5 mm), and the tops of 43 printed oboe staples (the 42 oboe rows of the oboe-shop.de list and the Reeds 'n Stuff page of the Chiarugi 2+ M, to 0.05 mm; several rows repeat a model) span 3.3 to 4.5 mm^2, median 3.7, with it. C_P = 0.8 is the one free parameter of their Fig. 15 fit (the other quantities held), and the authors note that it matches an extrapolation of Azad 1996's data on turbulent flow in a conical diffuser (half-angle 3.94 deg, Re 6.9e4). C_P 0.8 is extrapolated from turbulent conical-diffuser data at Re 5e4 and above; the staple's input runs at about 2e3 to 7e3 with an oscillating flow. Their text gives the staple's tapering angle as 5.2 deg and its L/d as 20, but that angle does not reproduce: their own Fig. 14 reads a half-angle of 1.34 deg (included 2.7 deg) between 28.5 and 70 mm, the 43 printed staples read 1.25 to 1.63 deg (median 1.50 deg; area ratios 3.4 to 5.1, L/d_in 20 to 23; the list prints no length, so 47 mm is taken, and 45 to 48 mm would give 1.2 to 1.7 deg), and this card's Table II cone is 1.51 deg, so the staple is a much gentler diffuser than the one 0.8 was extrapolated to. No diffuser data at its included angle (2.5 to 3.3 deg), length ratio or Reynolds number was found: the diffuser of the Manitoba group around Azad has a total angle of 8 deg and area ratio 4 (pipe-entry Re of 1.5e5 and 2.9e5 in the thesis of Okwuobi, 1972), a published loss correlation is valid for divergence angles from 5 deg and Re from 5e4, and an effectiveness relation for total angles of 6.8 to 30 deg and area ratios above 3. The input Reynolds number estimated from the D4 card's own blowing pressure (a Bernoulli jet through the reed gap, the reed open to 0.25 to 1 of its rest opening, viscosity assumed 1.87e-5 Pa s) is 1.8e3 to 7.2e3, and the Womersley number at the note is 12, so the flow is oscillatory and a constant C_P is an approximation. The law neglects the viscous loss along the reed, as this card does

The scale's tuning. Before the reed's closure stop the scale was flat because the reed passed through its lay; with it the notes sit -7 to +33 c from equal temperament, F4 plays an octave up in the second register (nothing was done to bring it back), and Bb4 sounds as B4 on the later page; the Bb4 page that plays, the 2026-11-04 render before the stop, sounds 59 c flat of equal temperament (450.6 Hz). The reed's blade mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed: they need the authors or a measured reed. A hunt of 11-08 found the blade inputs only in part. Gouged cane is about 0.60 mm thick at the centre and 0.45 mm at the sides, with 0.58 to 0.60 mm the gouging target (the pages of Hodge Products), and 0.58 to 0.59 mm for oboe-shop.de cane (a video description); the reed tips of Hodge's profiler templates are 6.6 to 7.0 mm wide; a 72 mm reed tied on a 47 mm staple (the same video description) leaves 25 mm of cane above the staple if the 72 mm runs from the tip to the staple's end. Blades of 25 to 28 mm by 6.4 to 7.0 mm have an area of 1.6 to 2.0 cm^2, so the 0.7 cm^2 face (a 28 x 6.4 mm blade times the uniform-cantilever weight 0.39) lies inside the 0.62 to 0.76 cm^2 these give; it stays. The 22 mg stays labelled borrowed from the clarinet: a blade at the gouged thickness everywhere has a tip-referenced effective mass of 18 to 28 mg (dry cane, 779 to 965 kg/m^3), so 22 mg lies inside that bound, which is not a derivation, because the scraped thickness profile and the density of wet cane were not found. The moduli found differ by a factor of 8 (3.1 GPa wet and 5.0 GPa dry on 1 mm specimens of saxophone reeds; 15 to 24 GPa on dry 0.5 mm strips), and a flat clamped-free beam of the found geometry and moduli has a stiffness of 10 to 1300 N/m, 3 to 350 times under the card's 3464 N/m, which comes from the measured closing pressure through P_c = k h0 / A: the card's lumped stiffness is not a flat blade's (a reason not tested here: the blade is a curved shell closing on its twin). Neither number was adjusted, and the damping, rest opening and closing pressure stay as labelled

The exterior is one flat infinite rigid baffle with a coplanar receiver in an inviscid gas: the bell and holes radiate as pistons in that baffle and the listener sits on its axis, while the recording does not share this geometry (the bell and holes radiate into free space and the listener is off any baffle plane); nothing has been run to show how much of the oboe's energy above 5 kHz this assumption carries.

A measured aeroacoustic noise level, spectrum and source strength of a reed-instrument jet: none was found, the constriction_noise row is a duct-obstruction trend borrowed outside its domain, and as delivered it sits 12 to 32 dB under the recording's floor at 1 to 4.5 kHz.
